result.topic: PAN-OS/Panorama XML+REST API request/response shapes, extracted from pan-python (xapi.py) and PaloAltoNetworks/pan-os-python (base.py, policies.py, objects.py, firewall.py) source code, to close "unconfirmed, pattern-guessed" gaps in pan_auth.py / pan_base.py / pan_firewall.py

confirmedFacts.claim: keygen response: API key is parsed at path result/key (i.e. XPath './result/key' from document root) — exactly matching pan_auth.py's current assumption.
confirmedFacts.evidence: self.element_result = self.element_root.find('result')  # can be None ... element = self.element_result.find('key') ... self.api_key = element.text  (xapi.py lines 285-286, 618-622)

confirmedFacts.claim: keygen request body is exactly type=keygen, user=<username>, password=<password> (form-encoded POST), with no other required fields.
op() (type=op) request params are exactly: type=op, cmd=<xml>, vsys=<optional>, key=<apikey>, and target=<serial> ONLY if a serial is set on the client.
confirmedFacts.evidence: query['type']='op'; if cmd: query['cmd']=cmd; if vsys: query['vsys']=vsys; query['key']=self.api_key; if self.serial is not None: query['target']=self.serial (xapi.py lines 939-947)

confirmedFacts.claim: License info op command string 'request license info' is exactly what the official Palo Alto Networks SDK sends, and it tokenizes to nested XML tags one-per-word (e.g. <request><license><info></info></license></request>), functionally identical to the prototype's hand-written <request><license><info/></license></request>.
confirmedFacts.evidence: def request_license_info(self): ... result = self.op("request license info") ... (base.py ~line 5439); op() default cmd_xml=True runs cmd through panos.string_to_xml() which wraps each whitespace-split token in matching open/close tags (panos/__init__.py string_to_xml, ~line 407)

confirmedFacts.claim: License op response is parsed at result/licenses/entry, with child elements feature, description, serial, issued, expires, expired, and ALSO authcode (prototype's parser is missing authcode). 'expired' is the literal string 'yes'/'no', not true/false — official SDK does `x.find('./expired').text == 'yes'`.
confirmedFacts.evidence: for x in result.findall("./result/licenses/entry"): ans.append(License(x.find('./feature').text, x.find('./description').text, x.find('./serial').text, ..., x.find('./expired').text == 'yes', x.find('./authcode').text))  (base.py, _format_result_as_license_list, ~lines 5404-5413)

confirmedFacts.claim: log() (type=log) initial submit sends exactly: type=log, key, log-type (optional), nlogs (optional), skip (optional), query=<filter as 'filter' param> (optional). It NEVER adds target=<serial>, even when the client's serial attribute is set — unlike op/config/commit/export/report/user_id, which all add target when serial is set.
confirmedFacts.evidence: def log(...): query={'type':'log','key':self.api_key}; if log_type: query['log-type']=log_type; if nlogs: query['nlogs']=nlogs; if skip: query['skip']=skip; if filter: query['query']=filter (xapi.py lines 1112-1124) -- no self.serial/target reference anywhere in the log() method (lines 1089-1170), contrasted with keygen (601-602), ad_hoc (679-680), __type_config (777-778), user_id (800-801), commit (868-869), op (946-947), export (1006-1007), report (1203-1204,1238-1239) which all check `if self.serial is not None: query['target']=self.serial`

confirmedFacts.claim: Log job polling uses a DIFFERENT completion signal than the prototype assumes: pan-python polls type=log&action=get&job-id=<id> and checks the text of result/job/status for the literal value 'FIN' to decide the job is done — it does NOT check for presence/absence of a <log> node.
confirmedFacts.evidence: job = self.element_root.find('./result/job') ... query={'type':'log','action':'get','key':self.api_key,'job-id':job.text} ... status = self.element_root.find('./result/job/status') ... if status.text == 'FIN': return  (xapi.py lines 1133-1159)

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-python's log() method never itself extracts individual log entries beneath <log> — it returns once status==FIN and leaves the caller to inspect element_root/xml_document. The exact nested entry path (e.g. result/log/logs/entry) is NOT exercised or asserted anywhere in pan-python's own source or its bundled CLI tool (panxapi.py just dumps the raw XML). This is a genuine, still-open gap, not an artifact of insufficient research.
confirmedFacts.evidence: xapi.log(log_type=..., nlogs=..., ...); print_status(xapi, action); print_response(xapi, options)  -- print_response only serializes xapi.xml_root()/xml_document, no per-entry parsing (panxapi.py ~lines 262-274)

confirmedFacts.claim: Panorama-to-firewall proxying (target=<serial>) is implemented end-to-end exactly as pan_base.py assumed for op/config: PanDevice.op() calls self.xapi.op(...); Firewall.generate_xapi() (when the Firewall object has a serial but no hostname, i.e. it's Panorama-managed) constructs its PanXapi with serial=self.serial using Panorama's own hostname/api_key/port; pan-python's PanXapi then adds target=<serial> automatically on op/config/commit/etc. calls per the fact above.
confirmedFacts.evidence: if self.serial is not None and self.hostname is None: kwargs = {'api_key': self.panorama().api_key, 'hostname': self.panorama().hostname, 'port': self.panorama().port, ..., 'serial': self.serial}  (firewall.py generate_xapi, ~lines 250-268)

confirmedFacts.claim: Security-profile attachment on a Security Rule is XML/tag-path profile-setting/group (a named Security Profile Group, vartype=member) OR profile-setting/profiles/<type> where <type> is one of virus, spyware, vulnerability, url-filtering, file-blocking, wildfire-analysis, data-filtering (each vartype=member, i.e. rendered as <member>name</member> children) -- these are mutually distinct modes (group vs individually-specified profiles), and BOTH exist as real, confirmed fields, resolving the prototype's open question of 'is it profile-setting.group or profile-setting.profiles.url-filtering' with 'it's whichever mode is configured, both are real fields.'
confirmedFacts.evidence: params.append(VersionedParamPath('group', path='profile-setting/group', vartype='member')); member_profiles = ('virus','spyware','vulnerability','url-filtering','file-blocking','wildfire-analysis','data-filtering'); for p in member_profiles: params.append(VersionedParamPath(p, vartype='member', path='profile-setting/profiles/{0}'.format(p)))  (policies.py, class SecurityRule, ~lines 459-483)

confirmedFacts.claim: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the task's framing: these per-type security-profile-attachment fields live in panos/policies.py's SecurityRule class, NOT in panos/objects.py. panos/objects.py's only profile-related class is SecurityProfileGroup (xpath '/profile-group' under the vsys root), which models the GROUP construct, not individual URL Filtering / Anti-Spyware / DNS Security profile objects. pan-os-python's objects.py and policies.py, as of the 'develop' branch, contain NO class named URLFilteringProfile, AntiSpywareProfile, VulnerabilityProfile, etc. at all -- there is no dedicated `panos/security_profiles.py` file in this repo either (confirmed 404 / absent from the GitHub API directory listing).
confirmedFacts.evidence: Directory listing of panos/ contains only: __init__.py, base.py, device.py, errors.py, firewall.py, ha.py, network.py, objects.py, panorama.py, plugins.py, policies.py, predefined.py, updater.py, userid.py -- no security_profiles.py; grep of objects.py's 19 classes (AddressObject...Edl) shows only SecurityProfileGroup as profile-related.

confirmedFacts.claim: SecurityProfileGroup (the profile-group object, i.e. what a rule's profile-setting/group member references) is at xpath suffix '/profile-group' under Root.VSYS, with member fields virus, vulnerability, url_filtering (XML path 'url-filtering'), spyware, wildfire_analysis etc. -- each vartype=member.
confirmedFacts.evidence: class SecurityProfileGroup(VersionedPanObject): ... self._xpaths.add_profile(value='/profile-group') ... params.append(VersionedParamPath('virus', path='virus', vartype='member')) ... params.append(VersionedParamPath('url_filtering', path='url-filtering', vartype='member')) (objects.py ~lines 682-725)

confirmedFacts.claim: A third-party (non-official, unofficial reconstruction) JSON schema of the PAN-OS security rule REST payload independently uses the IDENTICAL hyphenated field names and nesting found in the official SDK's XML paths: top-level 'profile-setting' object containing 'group' (list) and 'profiles' (object with keys virus, spyware, vulnerability, url-filtering, file-blocking, wildfire-analysis, data-filtering). This is a weak/tertiary source (not one of the two libraries the task specified, and not Palo Alto's own doc), but it corroborates -- rather than contradicts -- the XML-derived field names as the likely REST JSON shape too, since PAN-OS REST payloads are documented elsewhere to structurally mirror the XML config tree with the same key names.
confirmedFacts.evidence: "profile-setting" ... "group": List containing the name of a security profile group ...; "profiles": references IndividualProfiles with keys virus, spyware, vulnerability, url-filtering, file-blocking, wildfire-analysis, data-filtering

confirmedFacts.claim: Neither pan-python nor pan-os-python implement HTTP 429/Retry-After handling or 5xx exponential-backoff retry against the PAN-OS API. pan-python's __api_request treats ssl.CertificateError and URLError as terminal failures (sets status_detail, returns False -> raises PanXapiError), with zero retry. pan-os-python's only 'retry' concept (retry_on_peer) is HA active/passive failover triggered by classify_exception() on connection-level exceptions (timeout, URLError, TLS errors) -- never on an HTTP status code returned with a body. This means the prototype's pan_base.py _get_with_retry/_xml_request loop (429 + Retry-After, 5xx + exponential backoff) is an ORIGINAL design not modeled on, and not validated by, community practice -- whether PAN-OS actually emits 429 under load remains unconfirmed by any source found.
confirmedFacts.evidence: CONNECTION_EXCEPTIONS = (err.PanConnectionTimeout, err.PanURLError, err.PanOutdatedSslError, err.PanSessionTimedOut) ... classify_exception checks str(e).startswith('URLError:') / 'Invalid credentials.' / 'timeout waiting for job' / commit-in-progress strings -- no branch on HTTP status codes anywhere (base.py classify_exception, ~lines 4003-4075); xapi.py __api_request has no retry loop, only except/return False (xapi.py lines 528-545)

confirmedFacts.claim: pan-os-python literally subclasses pan-python's XML API client (class XapiWrapper(pan.xapi.PanXapi)) and wraps every public pan.xapi.PanXapi method (op, keygen, log, config get/set, etc.) with try/except + HA-failover logic, rather than reimplementing the wire protocol -- confirming pan-python's xapi.py is the de-facto, community-and-officially-relied-upon transport layer for PAN-OS's XML API, and that the two libraries' request shapes are one and the same, not independently-arrived-at conventions.
confirmedFacts.evidence: class XapiWrapper(pan.xapi.PanXapi): ... pan.xapi.PanXapi.__init__(self, *args, **kwargs) ... for name, method in inspect.getmembers(pan.xapi.PanXapi, pred): ... wrapper_method = PanDevice.XapiWrapper.make_method(name, method) (base.py ~lines 3860-3893)

remainingGaps: Exact literal 'Feature' string PAN-OS emits for the DNS Security subscription line inside <result><licenses><entry> -- neither library hardcodes any license feature names (they parse generically); still needs a live device or an official KB sample that happens to include a DNS Security-licensed box.

Exact nested XML path for individual log entries beneath a finished type=log job (e.g. result/log/logs/entry) -- confirmed to be genuinely unexercised by pan-python itself (its log() method and its own CLI tool panxapi.py never parse into individual entries, only dump raw XML), so this remains unconfirmed by the reference client, not just by our own research gap.

Whether PAN-OS actually returns HTTP 429 (or any HTTP-level rate-limit signal) under load -- absence of any 429/backoff handling in either widely-used library is suggestive but not proof either way; could mean PAN-OS doesn't rate-limit at the HTTP layer, or simply that no community contributor has needed to handle it yet.

The REST API JSON field names/casing for profile-setting/group and profile-setting/profiles/<type> are corroborated only by a third-party (non-Palo-Alto, non-community-SDK) reconstructed JSON schema, not by pan.dev, official docs, or either of the two libraries specified in the task (both are XML-API-based and never touch the REST surface) -- still needs live confirmation against a device's own /restapi-doc.

Individual security-profile object classes (URL Filtering, Anti-Spyware/DNS Security, Vulnerability, Antivirus, WildFire) are not modeled at all in pan-os-python's objects.py or policies.py as of the develop branch -- so this SDK provides zero corroboration (positive or negative) for the REST resource paths (Objects/URLFilteringSecurityProfiles, Objects/AntiSpywareSecurityProfiles) or their internal JSON field names that pan_firewall.py already uses; that specific gap is unchanged by this research pass.

Whether target=<serial> is rejected outright (HTTP/XML error) vs. silently ignored when sent on a type=log request -- we only confirmed the reference client never SENDS it for log(); we did not find any source (official docs, either SDK, or forum) describing what the PAN-OS server does if a caller manually adds target= to a type=log query string anyway.

No live device access in this research pass (network-search/source-code only, per task constraints) -- all findings above are 'confirmed by widely-used client source code' rather than 'confirmed by a live PAN-OS device response,' which is a materially weaker (though still strong) form of confirmation for the exact response envelope shapes.

recommendedCodeChanges.change: No change required. The ./result/key parsing in _generate_key() is now confirmed correct at HIGH confidence by pan-python's xapi.py (element_result = element_root.find('result'); key = element_result.find('key')). Update the module docstring's 'NOT CONFIRMED' note to 'CONFIRMED via pan-python xapi.py source' and drop the live-device caveat for this specific path.

In get_license_info(): the cmd string '<request><license><info/></license></request>' and the parse path './result/licenses/entry' are now confirmed correct at HIGH confidence (pan-os-python base.py request_license_info()/_format_result_as_license_list()). Add an 'authcode' field to the parsed entry dict (entry.findtext('authcode')) to match the official SDK's namedtuple. Also change how 'expired' is surfaced: store/interpret it as a boolean via `entry.findtext('expired') == 'yes'` (the official SDK does exactly this comparison) rather than passing through the raw string, since PAN-OS uses the literal token 'yes'/'no', not 'true'/'false'.

_xml_log_poll() currently decides a log job is finished purely by checking `root.find('./result/log') is None`. The reference client (pan-python) instead polls the SAME type=log&action=get&job-id=<id> request and checks `root.find('./result/job/status').text == 'FIN'` as the completion signal -- it never inspects a <log> node's presence/absence to decide pending-vs-done. Recommend adding a check on ./result/job/status text=='FIN' as the primary/authoritative completion signal (falling back to or cross-checking the <log>-node-presence heuristic only if status is absent), because a job that legitimately matched zero log entries could plausibly finish (status=FIN) without ever populating a <log> node -- which would make the current heuristic poll forever on an empty-result-set job. This is a real, concrete correctness risk introduced by not having a live device to test the zero-results case.

No signature change needed for _xml_log_submit/_xml_log_poll not accepting a `target` parameter -- this is now confirmed to match the reference client's behavior exactly (pan-python's log() method never adds target=<serial> even when serial is set on the client, unlike op/config/commit/export/report). Update the pan_api_research.md 'Open gap: whether target= works with type=log' entry from 'unconfirmed' to 'the reference client deliberately never sends it for log queries -- treat log-via-Panorama-proxy as unsupported by convention, not merely untested,' i.e. do not add a target passthrough to the log methods without first confirming against a live device that the server-side behavior differs from what every known client does.

In get_security_rules() / the module docstring's open gap about the URL Filtering profile-attachment field name on a rule: update the comment to state the field is one of TWO possible shapes depending on how the rule is configured -- profile-setting.group (a named Security Profile Group) OR profile-setting.profiles.url-filtering (an individually-attached URL Filtering profile) -- both confirmed as real XML paths in pan-os-python's SecurityRule class (policies.py). When parsing REST JSON responses, check for both `profile-setting.group` and `profile-setting.profiles.url-filtering` (and sibling profile types: virus, spyware, vulnerability, file-blocking, wildfire-analysis, data-filtering) rather than assuming a single field name; the REST JSON casing itself is only medium/low-confidence (corroborated by a third-party reconstructed schema, not by an official/SDK source), so still flag for live-device confirmation via /restapi-doc.

get_dns_security_profiles()/get_url_filtering_profiles(): no change recommended from this research pass -- neither pan-python nor pan-os-python touch the REST API or model individual security-profile objects at all (pan-os-python's objects.py only has the profile-GROUP construct), so this pass provides no additional confirmation or contradiction for these REST resource paths. Keep the existing 'needs live /restapi-doc confirmation' caveat as-is; do not upgrade its confidence based on this research.

Add a new section citing pan-python/pan-os-python source code (with the GitHub raw URLs used here) as a corroborating, code-level evidence tier between official docs and community forum posts. Explicitly record the retry-logic finding: neither library implements HTTP-status-based retry/backoff (429/5xx) -- the prototype's pan_base.py retry loop is original defensive code, not a confirmed PAN-OS behavior pattern, and should be labeled as such rather than implied-confirmed.
